picks.rationale: This is the largest effect size on the board: HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.25-0.45) in HRD-positive disease, and HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.28-0.66) in the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup that mirrors this patient, against the all-comer niraparib HR of 0.62. She is already on the bevacizumab backbone, so the only thing standing between her and the highest-upside maintenance regimen is one validated genomic-instability assay. I will champion ordering the Myriad MyChoice GIS now and committing to this regimen if it returns at least 42; below that threshold she is HRD-negative and this option closes. I am not pretending the eligibility is settled, only that the upside justifies forcing the GIS question instead of defaulting straight to niraparib.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is contingent on a GIS at least 42 she does not yet have; if it returns below 42 the regimen is foreclosed and the HR 0.33 never applies to her
Combination-arm grade 3+ AE near 57%, with grade 3+ hypertension 19% and anemia 17%, layered onto a patient with high VTE history and a prior IVC filter
Adds a PARP myelosuppression burden on top of bevacizumab's thrombotic and bleeding risk

picks.rationale: If the GIS comes back below 42, this is the bet I want: an all-comer label with no BRCA gate and no validated-score requirement, overall HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76) and HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.31-0.59) in the HRD-positive stratum. The preclinical pharmacology is unusually specific to her tumor: niraparib partitions into tumor at 3.3x plasma and cut growth 58% in a BRCA-wild-type PDX where olaparib barely moved (pmid:30647846), and it ranks among the strongest PARP trappers tested (pmid:23066039). It is oral and low-burden, which fits her stated preference. My honest reservation is that thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% at grade 3+ press directly on her severe-myelosuppression veto, mitigated but not erased by individualized starting dose.
primary_concerns: Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% sit on the patient's named severe-myelosuppression / febrile-neutropenia veto; individualized dosing reduces but does not remove this
Baseline WBC is already 3.5, a thin reserve for a myelosuppressive agent in a 70-79 age band
All-comer benefit is real but smaller than the HRD-positive-gated PAOLA-1 magnitude

picks.rationale: A second all-comer PARP maintenance with an ITT HR of 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68) that held in the HRD-negative stratum, so a BRCA-wild-type tumor qualifies without a BRCA gate, exactly like niraparib. The reason it sits behind niraparib rather than beside it is that I have no tumor-partitioning or trapping pharmacology pointing rucaparib at this specific BRCA-proficient biology, where niraparib carries that preclinical argument. Grade 3+ anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6% engage the same myelosuppression veto.
primary_concerns: Grade 3+ anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6% trigger the severe-myelosuppression veto, as with niraparib
Rucaparib is the redundant second all-comer PARP; its marginal edge over niraparib rests on board agreement rather than distinct biology
No biology-specific preclinical edge over niraparib in this BRCA-wild-type setting, so it is the redundant PARP rather than the lead one

picks.rationale: She is already on this and already at R0, and the OVATION 2 topline reads HR 0.79 for PFS (14.9 vs 11.9 mo) and HR 0.69 for OS, an OS signal large enough that I will not wave it off as a backbone afterthought. It works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment rather than the MSI/TMB checkpoint axis her MSS, TMB-low tumor forecloses, so the usual immunotherapy disqualifier does not apply here. The honest weaknesses are that this is early-phase data from a sponsor topline with CIs not reported and no peer-reviewed per-term safety table, and the magnitude trails the PARP options. I rank it as the clean continuation play: no veto triggered, IP delivery generally well tolerated, and it keeps a credible OS hypothesis alive while the GIS result decides the PARP question.
primary_concerns: Efficacy rests on a sponsor topline and a 2025 abstract; CIs are unreported and no peer-reviewed grade 3+ safety table is yet public
Smaller PFS effect than the PARP maintenance options, and the OS estimate is immature
Investigational status means access and continuity outside the trial structure are not guaranteed

notes: Risktaker ordering: I lead with the highest-magnitude option (PAOLA-1 olaparib+bev, HRD-positive HR 0.33) made contingent on forcing the MyChoice GIS, because she is already on bevacizumab and the only barrier is one assay. Niraparib is my fallback the moment the GIS reads below 42, and it carries the only tumor-specific preclinical pharmacology (Sun 2018 partitioning, Murai trapping) in a BRCA-wild-type tumor. Rucaparib is the redundant all-comer PARP (ITT HR 0.52). GEN-1 is the no-veto continuation with a real but immature OS signal. I did not rank letrozole (single ER-positive, PR-negative endocrine signal, serious-RoB retrospective evidence, magnitude too small for a rank-1-leaning persona to champion) or the PI3K/MAP2K4 phase-1 baskets (no validated benefit for amplification or MAP2K4 loss, no approved matched agent). SOLO1 olaparib monotherapy is foreclosed by BRCA-wild-type and is correctly excluded. The PARP picks all press on the severe-myelosuppression veto; I keep them because the maintenance benefit is large, but I flag the veto tension honestly rather than papering over it.
